newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish SPOiF broker plans to clear derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Polish SPOiF broker plans to clear derivatives.

text.p: Polish bank-owned System Pozagieldowego Obrotu Instrumentami Finansowymi SA (SPOiF) plans to establish its own clearing house to settle derivative contracts, the company's president said on Tuesday.
Jaroslaw Pachowski told a news conference that the clearing system was key to SPOiF's plan to expand from being a broker in secondary T-bill and NBP-bill trade.
"We have our own original plan to organise a clearinghouse if there is no central highly capitalised institution at the time we'll be ready to launch derivatives trade," he said.
But Pachowski did not rule out that SPOiF, which started operating as electronic broker on January 23, would cooperate with other institutions interested in organising derivatives trade.
Institutions interested in setting up a derivatives clearinghouse include the National Securities Depository (KDPW) and the Warsaw Commodities Exchange (WBOT).

SPOiF, established in April 1996, has 16 banks and Polish Banking Association as shareholders and a share capital of 1.625 million zlotys. It recorded a 14-million zloty turnover on Monday after a 30-million zloty trade on Friday.

SPOiF acts as an over-the-counter electronic broker now, and Lazarowicz did not elaborate whether SPOiF would seek a status of official exchange, approved by the Polish Securities Commission and government.
